Consult Summary:
- 31-year-old woman with ~2 months of progressive work-related anxiety characterized by morning panic, insomnia, daytime low mood/anhedonia, decreased activities, and intermittent palpitations; plan for talking-therapy referral, basic blood tests to exclude triggers, and GP follow-up.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Several months (approximately 2 months) of marked anxiety, worst in the mornings with dread about leaving house for work, resulting in difficulty getting out of bed.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Symptoms began ~2 months ago, coinciding with starting a new job in a retail head office.
  - Symptoms have worsened over the past two months.
- Exacerbating/initiating/relieving factors:
  - Initiating factor: starting new, stressful job; difficult relationship with boss.
  - Exacerbating: anticipation of going to work, public transport (tube) described as stressful.
  - No specific relieving factors documented.
- Associated symptoms / review of systems:
  - Sleep:
    - Bedtime ~22:00–23:00 but prolonged sleep latency; reports very shallow sleep, estimates 3–4 hours/night.
    - Frequently wakes before alarm with heart racing and panic about being late.
  - Cardiovascular:
    - Palpitations described as irregular, rapid heartbeats occurring in the morning with panic; duration variable from a couple of minutes up to ~10 minutes; no documented syncope.
    - No chest pain reported except discomfort/pain when heart racing.
  - Mood / Psychiatric:
    - Low mood, anhedonia (loss of enjoyment in previously enjoyable activities).
    - Anxiety pervasive, on edge most of the time.
    - No suicidal ideation or intent; has supportive family.
    - No prior comparable episodes reported.
  - Functional impact:
    - Avoidance of social activities; reduced participation in exercise (running, tennis).
    - Considering calling in sick frequently but has not missed work.
  - Appetite:
    - No significant change; increased chocolate/snacking noted.
  - Substance use:
    - Alcohol: reports drinking “quite a lot” on Fridays/Saturdays; occasional glass of wine during week; no quantified units documented.
    - Tobacco: occasional smoker.
    - Illicit drugs: denies use.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - Denies prior suicidal thoughts.
  - Denies prior similar severe episodes.
  - No chest pain consistent with ischemia documented.
  - No other systemic symptoms documented.

Past Medical History:
- No past medical conditions explicitly reported.
- Past psychiatric history: none reported by patient.
- Medications: none documented.
- Allergies: not documented.

Social History:
- Occupation: employed in head office team for a fashion retailer; new role in a new sector; describes job as very stressful and poor relationship with boss.
- Living situation: lives with parents.
- Alcohol: drinks frequently on weekends (described as “quite a lot” Fridays/Saturdays); occasional drinking during week; no quantity documented.
- Tobacco: occasional smoker.
- Recreational drugs: denies.
- Support: has family support; mother has past history of depression and is a source of support/advice.

Family History:
- Mother has a history of depression.
- No other family history documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: none documented.
- Examination findings: none documented.

Investigations:
- Plan documented to perform “a couple of basic blood tests” to exclude medical triggers for palpitations/anxiety; specific tests not listed.
- No imaging or test results available.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Anxiety with panic symptoms (provisional—most likely anxiety-related per clinician)
  - Assessment:
    - ~2 months of work-related anxiety with morning panic, anticipatory worry, avoidance behavior, daytime impairment, and low mood.
  - Plan:
    - Offer self-referral to NHS talking therapy (one-to-one therapy); clinician to provide referral link.
    - Provide online resources and information about sleep-hygiene strategies (clinician to add information to notes).
    - Advise patient to contact GP/support if anxiety worsens or she becomes unable to cope with work/normal activities.
    - Medication: clinician stated medications can be used for anxiety but would not be first-line at this stage (no medication prescribed).
- Issue 2: Insomnia / disturbed sleep
  - Assessment:
    - Marked sleep-onset insomnia and fragmented/shallow sleep with early morning awakening related to anxiety/panic.
  - Plan:
    - Provide written advice/resources on improving sleep (clinician to add to notes).
    - Manage underlying anxiety as above (talking therapy / resources).
    - Review at follow-up if sleep does not improve or worsens.
- Issue 3: Palpitations — likely anxiety-related but require exclusion of organic causes
  - Assessment:
    - Intermittent irregular rapid palpitations occurring primarily in the morning with panic; new over past ~2 months.
  - Plan:
    - Order basic blood tests to exclude triggers (tests not specified in transcript).
    - Arrange GP follow-up approximately 1 week after blood tests to review results.
    - Patient to contact support line to arrange blood tests (patient agreed to call).
    - Escalate if palpitations worsen or other cardiac symptoms develop.

- General plan items:
  - Clinician to send NHS talking-therapy self-referral link and online resource details.
  - Clinician to document sleep advice in medical notes.
  - Safety net: patient advised to return/call if unable to cope or symptoms escalate.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Allergies not documented.
  - Current medication list not documented (patient reported none, but reconciliation not explicit).
  - Vital signs and physical examination are absent.
  - Specific basic blood tests requested were not specified.
  - Quantified alcohol intake (units/week) not recorded.
  - Detailed past medical and psychiatric history not explicitly documented beyond patient statements.
  - No formal mental health risk assessment form documented (beyond verbal denial of suicidal ideation).
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - None identified.
- Transcript quality comment:
  - Transcript is generally clear and audible; minimal overlapping speech. Some lifestyle quantities (alcohol units) and exact tests were not specified.
